event: Nala answers him: her name is Nala, and she is from very far away.
She says she is not sure how she came here or even what here is, and asks them to set her right.

changes.note: Jory: her honest answer about far away earns 1
Wat: her honest answer about far away earns 1

memory.fact: Nala told the burners her name, that she is from far away, and unsure how she came here.
Nala told the burners her name, that she is from far away, and unsure how she came here.
Nala told the burners her name, that she is from far away, and unsure how she came here.

event: Jory lets her finish before he speaks; Wat turns his good ear towards her.

memory.fact: Wat is old, deaf in one ear, gruff, and will not have anyone go cold at his fire.
Wat is old, deaf in one ear, gruff, and will not have anyone go cold at his fire.

event: Jory answers her politely, and does not ask her twice about far away.

memory.fact: A stranger who speaks of far countries and no home is answered politely and watched quietly.

event: He tells her she is on the Carrow, which they call the Big Water, at the south edge of the Weald.

memory.fact: They call the Carrow the Big Water, and reckon Brackenford half a day down it by raft.
They call the Carrow the Big Water, and reckon Brackenford half a day down it by raft.

event: He reckons by burns and ridges, not miles: the Weald runs days north of here, all pine and hill.

memory.fact: A burner gives directions by burns, ridges and fords, never by miles, which he does not count.
A burner gives directions by burns, ridges and fords, never by miles, which he does not count.
The Weald runs days north of the Carrow, all pine and hill.
The Weald runs days north of the Carrow, all pine and hill.

event: West down the water lies Wenmarch, the town, and south across the river the Crown's country.

memory.fact: The river Carrow bounds the Weald on the south and flows west to the market town Wenmarch.
The river Carrow bounds the Weald on the south and flows west to the market town Wenmarch.
Weald folk speak of the Crown's country south beyond the river, and of Wenmarch as the town.
Weald folk speak of the Crown's country south beyond the river, and of Wenmarch as the town.

event: North above the pines are the Bare Backs, and he says plainly that nothing lives up there.

memory.fact: Weald folk call the bare fells north of the trees the Bare Backs and say nothing lives up there.
Weald folk call the bare fells north of the trees the Bare Backs and say nothing lives up there.

event: Wat puts in that the wolves hold the middle of the Weald, and nobody crosses it after dark.

memory.fact: Wolves hold the Weald's middle, and folk do not cross it after dark.
Wolves hold the Weald's middle, and folk do not cross it after dark.

event: Wat says the bear came down off the fells this autumn; the east slopes are no place alone.

memory.fact: Locals fear the bear on the east slopes this autumn and go nowhere near them alone.
Locals fear the bear on the east slopes this autumn and go nowhere near them alone.

event: He says the nearest who can do for a hurt foot is the herb-wife at Brackenford, half a day down.

memory.fact: Neither is a healer; the nearest is the herb-wife at Brackenford, half a day on downstream.
Neither is a healer; the nearest is the herb-wife at Brackenford, half a day on downstream.

event: Jory says the raft will not go down till the burn is out, and that is five days off.

memory.fact: Jory Tull and old Wat are charcoal burners, at the clamp five more days, then rafting home.
Jory Tull and old Wat are charcoal burners, at the clamp five more days, then rafting home.

event: Wat takes her cut foot onto his knee and works pine-tip salve into it with a hard thumb.
It stings like fire, and then the foot is easier than it has been all day.

changes.note: Pine-tip salve on her cut foot by the fire: HP 4 → 6

memory.fact: Wat worked pine-tip salve into Nala's cut foot and wrapped it; it stung, then eased.
Wat worked pine-tip salve into Nala's cut foot and wrapped it; it stung, then eased.
Wat worked pine-tip salve into Nala's cut foot and wrapped it; it stung, then eased.
Wat worked pine-tip salve into Nala's cut foot and wrapped it; it stung, then eased.

event: He wraps it in cloth, and says she will not wear that out in a morning's walking.

changes.note: An hour fed, warm and sitting still by the fire: SP 7 → 15

event: Jory pulls his shovel onto his shoulder and goes back out to tend the clamp.
At the doorway he says the gate at Brackenford will want a name, a village and a road.

memory.fact: A stranger naming no village and no road is reckoned a runaway or an outlaw, and spoken round.
A stranger naming no village and no road is reckoned a runaway or an outlaw, and spoken round.

event: He says a stranger with no village is held a runaway there, as one plain thing among others.

memory.fact: Brackenford's gate asks a stranger's name, village and road; one with no village is held a runaway.
Brackenford's gate asks a stranger's name, village and road; one with no village is held a runaway.

event: Wat spits into the fire and looks at her across it for a while.
He asks her straight out, the way he would ask about weather, whether anybody is hunting her.
